note: Authored by a single scheduled automated session playing both roles in one pass (hourly automation) — not two independent live API calls like a manual `python backrooms.py` run.

turns.text:
Concrete ramp slopes up into dark, oil-black puddles catching sodium light in broken slabs. Paws test the first stair-lip of a parking structure long since given up by cars — cold concrete, gum-dark stains, a smell of rust and old exhaust gone stale as dust. Ears swivel to the low groan of the structure itself, metal settling somewhere far above.

Nose drops to a support pillar, reads it slow. Old piss-mark, faded, weeks stale. Then, layered over it, fresher — sharp, deliberate, a stripe of scent scraped high on the concrete. Not this crew's ground. Someone's claimed it since.

the mark is three days old, maybe four, laid by a big tom with a torn ear who runs the upper decks for a crew that calls itself nothing, just claims things by scraping them raw

structure breathes around you — seven levels of empty concrete, rebar showing through crumbled edges where the corp that built it stopped paying maintenance two winters back, left the whole tower half-swallowed by its own decay

water drips somewhere on level three, steady, patient, pooling black under a blown-out light fixture that hasn't held a bulb in years

far up, past the ramps, a generator hums — building's last live circuit, feeding something nobody bothers to name, keeping one red emergency light blinking slow at the very top like a heartbeat nobody's checking on

wind funnels down the open ramp-mouths, carries city-smell in gusts — rain, ozone, distant fry-oil, and under it all, cold and mineral, the specific nothing-smell of a building nobody wants anymore

Weight shifts back off the claimed pillar, not a challenge, just information filed away. Paws carry forward along the wall-line instead, staying low, staying wide of open floor where the sodium light through broken windows would show a shape moving.

The drip on level three pulls at the ear more than the nose — water means something, this deep in a dead building, worth knowing where. Body moves toward the stairwell mouth in that liquid unhurried crawl, pausing at each pillar to scent-check before crossing open ground.

stairwell smells of cold iron and pigeon, feathers ghosted into corners, one skeleton picked clean long ago and gone to dust and calcium under a stripped car battery someone left charging nothing

step down, step down, each one echoing thinner than it should in an empty stairwell, sound doing what sound does in concrete boxes — bouncing, multiplying, lying about how loud you are

level three opens up wide and gray, water black-pooling under the dead fixture just like the drip promised, ripples going out slow and perfect from each drop, no wind reaching this deep to break the pattern

near the puddle: a cable, thick as a wrist, snaking up out of a maintenance hatch and into the dark, sheathing split and sparking faint blue-white every few seconds, not dangerous exactly, just tired, just old, humming its own small song into the concrete that vibrates faint up through paw-pads

Paw lifts away from the vibrating patch of floor fast, instinct first, thought second. The blue-white spark reads as wrong-light, not-fire, not-food, filed under leave-alone. Body arcs wide around the puddle instead, careful not to let a paw break the water's stillness and send a splash-sound echoing up the open stairwell shaft.

Nose swings past the pigeon-bones without interest — too old, too dry, no threat and no meal either. What pulls harder is a draft coming from the level above, carrying something warmer. Ears prick, then the whole head tilts toward the ramp leading up.

the draft rides down from level four, warmer because level four still has half a wall of glass left in it, catching afternoon sun for hours before the structure's shadow finally swallowed it — residual warmth baked into concrete, fading now but still real against a cold nose

ramp up is steep, water-stained in a long dark tongue where rain's found a way in through the broken glass and run downhill for longer than anyone's been counting

halfway up, another mark — this one wet-fresh, laid an hour ago at most, torn-ear tom's scent sharp enough to make whiskers twitch back

somewhere above, metal shifts, deliberate, not settling-groan but weight-on-metal, something moving that isn't wind and isn't rain

far off through the broken glass wall, city-glow bleeds orange-pink across the ramp's water-tongue, and a security drone's rotor thrums two structures over, sweeping its usual bored circuit, searchlight not yet swung this way

Body drops flat against the ramp's low wall at the fresh mark, breath gone shallow and quiet. The weight-on-metal sound above pins both ears forward, pupils blowing wide even in the ambient orange spill. Not fleeing yet — this deck isn't claimed by scent laid *this* fresh unless someone's still on it.

Paws creep the last stretch of ramp low and slow, staying in the water-tongue's shadow where the wet concrete doesn't catch light. Nose works overtime, trying to place the shifting-metal sound against the drone-thrum outside — different rhythm, closer, heavier than rotor.

level four opens through the broken glass wall into full city-view, towers stacked block on block into the rain-haze, windows lit in a thousand indifferent little squares, and somewhere among them the torn-ear tom sits on an overturned oil drum, weight-on-metal sound explained — just him, shifting his perch, tail curled tight, watching the same skyline you are

he hasn't smelled you yet, wind's wrong for it, blowing his scent down toward you instead of yours up toward him

the drone outside swings its searchlight in a slow arc, catching the broken glass wall in one long white sweep — for half a second everything in the room goes stark and shadowless, drum, tom, rain-streaks on concrete, you, all of it lit flat and total

then the beam slides on, hunting some other rooftop, and the dark folds back in, softer now, eyes taking a moment to trust it again

/\/\_/\/\
    (  O   O  )
     \  ^Y^  /
      )=====(      -- ears up, rotor incoming --

Body freezes mid-crouch through the drone's sweep, every muscle locked, not even a whisker moving — stillness the only defense against a light that doesn't care what it finds. The beam passes without catching, and only then does breath resume, slow and controlled through the nose.

Eyes stay locked on the tom's silhouette against the tower-glow. No challenge in the body — ears aren't pinned, tail isn't lashing, just low and reading. This deck's claimed and the claim's still warm on the drum. Retreat costs nothing here; the water-tongue and stairwell are already memorized as the way back down.

the retreat goes unnoticed, torn-ear tom still watching the skyline, some private vigil of his own, ears occasionally flicking to the drone's distant thrum but never once turning toward the stairwell shadow where a smaller shape unspools itself backward, paw over paw, silent as the water it skirted on the way up

back down the ramp, back past the wet-fresh mark, back past the sparking cable's blue-white pulse still ticking its tired rhythm into the concrete

stairwell swallows the retreat whole, pigeon-dust and cold iron indifferent to who passes through

level two, when it comes, is different — lower, closer to street-hum, a corner of the deck walled off by a collapsed section of ceiling that's made a rough den of rubble and rebar, and tucked into it: a nest of shredded cardboard and insulation foam, old, but not abandoned-old, still holding a warm-body smell that isn't torn-ear tom's

Nose drops into the rubble-den's mouth, sorting the smell layer by layer — not tom, not threat-shaped at all, softer, smaller, kit-smell maybe, old milk-scent ghosted into the foam. Body doesn't enter yet, just noses the threshold, reading whether anyone's home.

The den's shape pulls at something older than caution — shelter, dry, walled on three sides by fallen concrete, the fourth side facing away from the open ramp where rain and drone-light both fail to reach. Paws test the cardboard's edge, weight held light, ready to back out at the first sound that isn't settling structure.

den's empty, has been for a day or two — kit-smell fading under dust already settling back over the foam, whoever nested here moved on, maybe grew, maybe got carried off by something bigger, maybe just wandered toward a better corner, no way to know and the den doesn't say

rebar overhead makes a rough lattice roof, rain finding only a few thin lines through it, most of the space bone-dry, warmer than the open deck by degrees that matter

street-hum three floors down comes muffled through the collapsed wall — traffic-hiss, a distant vendor's cart wheel squeaking, someone's radio bleeding tinny pop-static through a cracked window somewhere

no drone reaches this low, no torn-ear scent this far down, no fresh threat in the dust

just an empty, dry, defensible corner, waiting on whoever claims it next

Body circles the nest once, twice, pressing weight into the cardboard to test its give, working the foam into a shape that fits — not the last tenant's shape, this one's own. Paws knead once, twice, the old instinct surfacing even half-starved and city-worn. Then the crouch folds down into it, spine curving to the rubble-wall's angle, tail wrapping close.

Ears keep their slow check-check rhythm even settling in — street-hum below, structure-groan above, the far thin thread of the generator's hum bleeding down through seven levels of dead concrete. None of it close. None of it now.

rebar-lattice roof holds its thin rain-lines steady, ticking soft against fallen concrete, a rhythm no different from any other roof in the city, just older, just quieter, just claimed now by something small and patient

generator hum thins to background thread, emergency light blinking its slow red heartbeat seven floors up, unseen from here, unbothered either way

dust settles slow around the nest, kit-ghost-smell fading further under warmer, closer, present scent laid fresh into the foam with every shift of weight

rotor sound passes far off again, three structures over now, hunting some other deck, some other shadow, and it fades to nothing worth flinching at

street-hum keeps its distant tide going, vendor-cart wheel still squeaking its same worn note, radio-static still bleeding its same tinny half-song, all of it folding into one long indifferent city-breath that doesn't reach this dry rubble corner at all

Eyes half-lid, tracking the thin rain-lines through the rebar without urgency, the same loose readiness as every other watch before sleep — ready to snap alert, in no hurry to. Paw drags once over muzzle, over ear, the grooming stroke of a body deciding the corner's safe enough to bother.

Tail curls tighter around haunches. The claimed deck upstairs, the torn-ear tom, the drone's searchlight — all of it filed away as someone else's floor, someone else's problem, three levels up and none of it this den's business tonight.

Breath slows. Structure keeps its old groan going somewhere far above, patient as the dripping puddle two floors up. The nest holds warm, holds dry, holds still.

structure settles into its long nightly creak, concrete cooling by degrees nobody's counting, rebar ticking faint as it contracts, the whole dead tower breathing its slow mineral breath around one small claimed corner

rain keeps its thin lattice-rhythm going overhead, missing the nest by design now, water finding its old paths down through cracks that have nothing to do with this dry patch of foam

generator hum threads on seven floors up, red light blinking its patient unwatched heartbeat, keeping its lonely vigil over a building that stopped needing it years ago and never told it to stop

street-hum below rises and falls with the hour, cart-wheel gone quiet now, radio-static finally cutting to dead air, city settling toward its own smaller hours

and here, in a rubble-walled den three floors above street level, seven below sky —

one small shape breathes slow

claimed, dry, unbothered

night keeps moving around it, the way it always does, the way it doesn't need permission to
